title: decoder-interleave-warp-scratchpad
content:
Goal:
- Short, repeatable notes to reproduce an intermittent long-context decoder failure. Focus: interleaving of KV updates between decoder kernels + attention kernel selection under very long sequence lengths (>= 12k).

Symptoms observed:
- Occasional token corruption at seq positions near 8k/16k boundaries (alphabetic garbage inserted).
- Repro rate ~1-3% when running synthetic long prompts (deterministic prompt + streaming) on ded-dev machines.
- No heap OOM; memory accounting looks fine. Latency spikes correlate with kernel fallback to 'attn_fallback'.

Quick repro (local, short):
1) python experiments/long_context_runner.py --model rwd-gpt-7b --prompt-file tests/long_prompts/12k_boundary.txt --batch 1 --max-seq 16384 --kv-mode interleave --kernel-hint auto
2) Observe corruption after ~ 20-60k tokens generated.

Commands I've run and logs collected:
- Start with small reproduce loop:
  for i in `seq 1 200`; do 
    ./bin/serve_infer --model rwd-gpt-7b --seq 16384 --kv-interleave=1 --kernel-select=auto --seed 42 
  done 2>&1 | tee runs/rep_loop.log
- Grep for 'CORRUPT' marker injected into runtime:
  grep -n "CORRUPT" runs/rep_loop.log | head
- Sample error snippet (from run 87):
  [2026-02-28T14:12:10Z] ERROR runtime: token mismatch at pos 8192 (expected 0x61 got 0x3f) ctx-id=5f3d
  stack: serve->decoder_layer_11->kv_write->attn_kernel_v2_fallback

Hypotheses (rough):
A) KV interleave write ordering race: when decoder layers write KV shards in an interleaved fashion (layer0 writes shard0, layer1 writes shard1, ...), a scheduling preemption can cause later attention kernel to read stale slots if offsets are updated in-place without atomic barriers.
B) Kernel selection mismatch: autotuner picks different kernels for chunks (e.g., attn_fused for short prefixes, attn_v2 for long tails). When switching mid-request, sharded KV offsets used by the former kernel layout differ from the latter layout. No migration step -> mismatch.
C) Wraparound offset arithmetic: offsets maintained as 32-bit signed ints; with seq>8192 we hit a branch that uses signed compare and produce negative effective index for lookups in some kernel paths. This is rare until context cross a power-of-two boundary.

What I tried (and results):
- Forcing kernel to attn_fused (env KERNEL_FORCE=attn_fused): repro -> 0/200. Good signal that kernel-switch matters.
- Forcing kernel to attn_v2: repro -> 4/200 (lower but not zero).
- Disable interleave (kv-interleave=0 -> contiguous per-layer writes): repro -> 0/200. Suggests interleave pattern strongly correlated.
- Add an explicit memory barrier (patched runtime to atomic_store on KV offsets) locally: repro -> 1/200. Reduced but not eliminated; possible missing fences in native kernels.
- Change KV slot type from int32 to uint64 (quick compile variant): repro -> 0/200. This is interesting; suggests sign/overflow bug in offset math.

Instrumentation notes (what to capture next):
- Add per-request KV-offset checksum (simple XOR of last 8 slots) at decoder enter/exit; log mismatch with kernel id. Aim: detect mismatch point in production.
- Trace kernel selection decisions (tied to sequence length heuristic) and log <request, kernel_selected, step, kv-offset-snapshot> to ephemeral tracing stream.
- Enable GPU buffer dump on mismatch: dump first 128 bytes of KV shard that was read and last write timestamp.

Repro plan (narrow):
1) Rebuild runtime with KERNEL_DEBUG=1 and KV_OFF_CHECKSUM=1.
2) Run long_context_runner but with --pin-core to reduce preemption noise.
3) Run 1000 iterations on ded-dev-2 (same HW that triggered original incident). Collect traces.
4) If mismatch detected, reproduce with smaller synthetic model (tiny toy model) to get deterministic low-level trace.

Possible fixes (ranked):
- Short: Force contiguous KV writes when seq > 4096 (workaround).
- Medium: Add atomic fences/explicit memory barriers around KV offset updates and ensure kernels use same packing/endianness.
- Long: Unify kernel layouts or add a migration shim when switching kernel mid-request that rewrites KV to expected layout.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Do some GPUs reorder writes in a way that looks like our interleaved pattern is non-atomic across warps? Need CUDA mem ordering reference.
- Is there any interaction with quantization (int8 kernels) that use different packing which could be misinterpreting offsets?
- Could the batcher (continuous batching) be merging partial KV writes from adjacent requests? Logs currently indicate single-request only, but need to double-check batcher boundary condition code.

Next quick experiments (priority):
- A: Run with KERNEL_FORCE=attn_fused on prod-sim for 24h, monitor regression and perf delta. Low risk; temporary mitigation.
- B: Reproduce in small toy with explicit warp-level sync removed to see if race appears.
- C: Add uint64 offset experiment to ded-dev (compile flag) and test 2000 runs.

Snippets of investigative code (local):
- checksum patch: (pseudocode)
  uint64_t kv_checksum(const KVHeader *h) { uint64_t x=1469598103934665603ULL; for (i=0;i<8;i++) x ^= h->slots[i]; return x; }
  log("kv_ck_before=%016x kernel=%s", kv_checksum(h), kernel_name);
- kernel select logging (C):
  if (kernel_hint==AUTO) trace_event("kernel_pick", req_id, seq_len, chosen_kernel_name);

Anything else I should capture here?
- I want to add which exact compiler flags we used for the failing build; currently recorded in CI artifact GH-PR-4321.
- Also plan to ask SRE for perf-counter dumps around memcopy ops (copy H2D/D2H).

Random notes / for later:
- The corruption pattern tends to flip punctuation characters near 8191 index; might hint at off-by-one in memcpy sizes (copy length = seq_len * sizeof(slot) possibly missing +1).
- If we cannot fully eliminate, consider automatic fallback to safe kernel and degrade latency but avoid corruption.

END - keeping this as a lightweight scratchpad to iterate.
